title: SHE BROKE THE JAR.
paragraphs:
Not by accident.
Not by clumsiness.
Because some worship cannot stay sealed.

Dinner is on the table.
Laughter in the air.
The smell of roasted food.
And sitting there like any other guest…
The same Jesus who just raised her brother from the grave.
The same Jesus who called “Lazarus, come out.” (John 11:43)
But Mary of Bethany is remembering.

Remembering the tomb.
Remembering the grief.
Remembering the miracle.

An alabaster jar of pure nard.
Perfume worth a year’s wages. (John 12:5)

One moment of devotion…
that cost everything.
The fragrance explodes into the room.
She pours the perfume on Jesus’ feet.
In that culture, a woman never did that in public.
But Mary doesn’t care about reputation anymore.
She wipes His feet with her hair.

“Why wasn’t this perfume sold and the money given to the poor?”
— John 12:5

“He did not say this because he cared about the poor but because he was a thief.”
— John 12:6
In Greek, it carries the force of “Stop bothering her.”
Mary understood something the disciples missed.

So before the nails…
before the thorns…
before the tomb…
And here’s the part that grips me.
Because once the jar is broken…
What jar are you still protecting?

Your reputation?
Your comfort?
Your secret sin?
Your control?
Jesus is worth more than the perfume.

More than approval.
More than dignity.
More than money.
Broken on a cross for sinners like us.

“This is my body, which is for you.”
— 1 Corinthians 11:24
Mary poured perfume on His feet.
Jesus would pour His blood for the world.
Give Jesus the devotion you’ve been holding back.
Because the fragrance of a surrendered life?
And heaven never calls it waste.
Someone out there thinks their devotion is too messy, too costly, too late.
